title: restic prune fails and reports missing data
body:
Third attempt -- hope nothing the message stays intact this time.

Output of `restic version`
--------------------------

restic 0.18.1 compiled with go1.25.1 on linux/amd64


What backend/service did you use to store the repository?
---------------------------------------------------------

Backblaze

Problem description / Steps to reproduce
----------------------------------------

 * A description of the problem you are having with restic.

While trying to do a prune I got the message

```
 echo <my password> | restic prune
reading repository password from stdin
repository 24395474 opened (version 1)
loading indexes...
[0:10] 100.00%  422 / 422 index files loaded
loading all snapshots...
finding data that is still in use for 170 snapshots
[1:02] 100.00%  170 / 170 snapshots
searching used packs...
{<data/68dcccd1> <data/8381da02> <data/dc8ff396> <data/1a05666c> <data/1adb5bca> <data/acfe2f5f> <data/3beb72e0> <data/658c9f6b> <data/bda267e7> <data/e969788b> (157 more)} not found in the index

Integrity check failed: Data seems to be missing.
Will not start prune to prevent (additional) data loss!
Please report this error (along with the output of the 'prune' run) at
https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/new/choose
Fatal: index is not complete
```

 * The complete command line and any environment variables you used to
   configure restic's backend access. Make sure to replace sensitive values!

The command line was 

```
 echo <my password> | restic prune
```

I think the only relevant envariables are

```
RESTIC_REPOSITORY=b2:restic-home-dir
B2_ACCOUNT_KEY=<will provide if needed>
```

 * The output of the commands, what restic prints gives may give us much
   information to diagnose the problem!

Prior to this I had run 

```
 echo <my password> | restic rewrite  --forget --exclude '/home/<user>/*mp4'  debb92eb a41efd49 5eca21e6 cbbfb5e6 8aff207b 28e9e08d d590ff89 dc40da96 311d4341 75babc62 a122ba04 b186109d 637882a5 af0ccbea b45fb81e 71d182d0 03c5399a d646362b 4e1aa40f 8349891f 48637778 8511ecb9 261d49c2 73b38344 5c4635e9 41d7a5e1 96ed323e a465f64b 6f3dd946 f3e13397 a2368ead f946d16c 77958782
```

And prior to that I ran

```
echo <my password> | restic repair  snapshots a0cf0c51 519684df e61be390 ef70d310 b6b3ecdb 5a9111ee c29a2b4a dcdd1725 0932f219 9123d961 a7f34e92 a4704ead 42eb489b da99a0b2 52cf0a65 32f6e44c 988642ba 52339bc5 119a3508 91572b20 3e256265 fbdd65fa 6b508d97 978dc070 4cadcd2c 31f6d1ca b5d8fbb2 36c92e98 6128081d 242054d7 7e13ff2f eaf42b33 2d7d7432 --forget 
```

because otherwise the rewrite commands would always fail with messages like
Fatal: unable to rewrite snapshot ID "a899a76c": cannot encode tree at "/home/<user>/MSRI/MacStuff/Library" without losing information

which I presume were due to the fact that all the snapshots were done under restic 0.12, and I only upgraded to 0.18 yesterday in order to be able to use the  rewrite command introduced in 0.13.


Expected behavior
-----------------


Well, I expected the prune to go through and tell me how much space has been saved.  (I had done a prune successfully after a repair/rewrite cycle on a handful of snapshots as a test, but I didn't keep their numbers.)

Actual behavior
---------------
The prune fails with the message copied near the top of this form:
Integrity check failed: Data seems to be missing.
Will not start prune to prevent (additional) data loss!
Please report this error (along with the output of the 'prune' run) at
https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/new/choose
Fatal: index is not complete


Do you have any idea what may have caused this?
-----------------------------------------------

After the small (and successful) repair/rewrite/prune cycle that I ran as a test, I realized I'd need to "repair" all snapshots and tried to do that with the command

 echo <my password> | restic repair snapshots

I interrupted this operation (I think because it was doing them in random order and I wasn't sure that was the right thing, because it went silent for a long time after reporting the repair of a few snapshots).  

Interrupting it shouldn't have caused corruption, but perhaps it did?  
Here is that last output for that omnibus repair command:

snapshot 0932f219 of [/home/<user>] at 2021-06-22 03:36:23.240036018 -0700 PDT by levy@participant3
  C-c C-csignal interrupt received, cleaning up
could not load snapshots: context canceled
Fatal: unable to rewrite snapshot ID "0932f219": context canceled




Did restic help you today? Did it make you happy in any way?
------------------------------------------------------------
The documentation for the rewrite feature was very clear and well-written:
restic.readthedocs.io/en/stable/045_working_with_repos.html#removing-files-from-snapshots
and until the error message above things seemed to be working as intended.  I hope the error is not a sign of some permanent damage.

Thank you

Silvio Levy

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hi Silvio,

I am reading your report and I wonder what ``restic check`` will tell you. I also wonder how large your repository is. I personally would use ``restic stats --mode debug`` to answer this question. This will give you a distribution of the various types of files in your repository.  
I know you have got 170 snapshots and 422 index files. Your repository is a "version 1" repo. Migration to "version2 "? Depending on size this might take a while - but not now, since you might have a broken repository.
 
So to repeat:
```
restic check --verbose=2
restic stats --mode debug
```

See https://restic.readthedocs.io/en/stable/077_troubleshooting.html#troubleshooting of how to use ``restic check``.
Copy the full output of these command in a file and attach them to your issue. Make sure they end in .txt; github is very peculiar which file types you can upload. 

If ``restic check --read-data`` ends with '``no errors were found``' you can safely assume that the repository is sound and healthy. However, ``restic check --read-data`` may take a long time, depending on your connection speed to your repository and the size of it. ``restic check`` and '``no errors were found``' tells you that the structure of the repository is sound, and you may assume that all is well.

Afterwards I would be inclined to run ``restic repair index --read-all-packs`` to gather the missing blobs and insert them into the master index. But I would like to see your diagnostic outputs first.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hi Silvio,
That's a bummer - a broken repository. I hope you have some additional backup for your data.

The two packfiles definitely need to be repaired:
``restic repair packs f3ade64cdd31ea7697ad1a9831a09d7e2f93df83f526e68c025f66d7791f3acd 1ed8c1dd8c0f0035279b17f0b1476fab2303830857f60de55d725ed80f7404e1``.

The help message says: ``The "repair packs" command extracts intact blobs from the specified pack files, rebuilds
the index to remove the damaged pack files and removes the pack files from the repository.`` Because the actual length of these two packfiles is larger than expected length, you should not loose much (I hope).

The next step I would undertake is the ``restic repair index``. (See also WARNING below). This command will step through all the packfile headers and will add missing index entries. 

Your tree node ``f63d7a881a585ff2681b0a62f991328c2e280db3a96faa42ec72eee486177cad`` is probably still be damaged. This node has about 150 node entries.

Here is the help text for ``restic repair snapshot``:
```
The "repair snapshots" command repairs broken snapshots. It scans the given
snapshots and generates new ones with damaged directories and file contents
removed. If the broken snapshots are deleted, a prune run will be able to
clean up the repository.

!!!The command depends on a correct index, thus make sure to run "repair index"
first!!!!  (The exclamation marks are mine)


WARNING
=======

Repairing and deleting broken snapshots causes data loss! It will remove broken
directories and modify broken files in the modified snapshots.

If the contents of directories and files are still available, the better option
is to run "backup" which in that case is able to heal existing snapshots. Only
use the "repair snapshots" command if you need to recover an old and broken
snapshot!
```

I don't know if you still have the original files and directories for ``D3A15DF306F350B779C972C8D800137BB415C4F1`` to ``D6882F409FD6B5C18E3B4333FDC26CB3E19682C5``. If the files still exist, try a backup of these missing files first. 

Before you start with ``restic repair snapshots --forget`` I strongly recommend to do another ``restic check``. 

Please let me know how you are proceeding.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: In case you want to investigate the tree structure of your snapshots further, you could use a pull request which I have submitted recently: https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/5678. Extract the file ``cmd/restic/cmd_cat.go``, replace the existing one, run ``make`` and you have your own ``restic`` module ready. The syntax is ``restic cat full-tree <snapshot-id>`` It generates the whole tree in JSON format. The output is sorted in ``path`` order.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> Interrupting it shouldn't have caused corruption, but perhaps it did?
> Here is that last output for that omnibus repair command:

Interrupting `restic repair snapshots` is fine. In the worst case it leaves some garbage data behind, but won't damage the repository.

> Afterwards I would be inclined to run `restic repair index --read-all-packs` to gather the missing blobs and insert them into the master index. But I would like to see your diagnostic outputs first.

Running the `restic repair packs ...` command printed by `check` will likely have roughly the same effect but is much faster, so I'd try `restic repair packs ...`  first.

The `unexpected file size` lines look a lot like the index for those files is incomplete. This could happen at some relatively old restic version (maybe restic 0.12 or even earlier), but won't happen any longer. So most likely this particular damage already happened at some point far in the past. Did you run `prune` or `check` from time to time?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Looking at your 260218-restic-errors.txt, you removed the broken packfile successfully. 

The next steps would indeed be:
> restic repair index
restic backup --exclude-caches /home/<user>
restic check

The one thing you could do  to find out more about these missing files like
> error for tree f63d7a88:  
tree f63d7a881a585ff2681b0a62f991328c2e280db3a96faa42ec72eee486177cad: file "D3A15DF306F350B779C972C8D800137BB415C4F1" blob ...

is to do find it with the linux ``find`` command:
> find /home/<user> -name "D3A15DF306F350B779C972C8D800137BB415C4F1" . 
The hard-core version of it will be ``sudo find ...``, if you get ``permisson denied`` errors.
 
If there is a result at all you will see a line (or lines)
``./intermediate/subdirectories/D3A15DF306F350B779C972C8D800137BB415C4F1``, then you will know that ``intermediate/subdirectories`` represents your tree ``f63d7a881a585ff2681b0a62f991328c2e280db3a96faa42ec72eee486177cad``. Make sure that  ``intermediate/subdirectories`` will be included in your backup.

I am not very hopeful, that ``restic find D3A15DF306F350B779C972C8D800137BB415C4F1`` will produce any meaningful output. 

Regarding ``restic repair index``:
The index is central to the workings of restic: what cannot be found in the index does not exist! The ``restic repair index`` is harmless, since it does not modify your backed up data in any way, shape or form. But if it finds a blob (=some data) which wasn't in the index before, it will add it. Therefore an up-to-date index is essential. Normally the index gets updated automatically, but you can always give the index a helping hand.

comments.body:
Hi Silvio,

If you think that they are Mozilla cache files, these are long gone. And it is not worth persuing them. I personally have a list of files which I exclude from the backup, and use ``restic backup --exclude-file excluded-files ..`` for that. 

>It's not rare that during a restic backup some files get deleted, and
restic reports them as missing. Could it be that this causes the repo
to be corrupt? If so, that would explain how I go into this mess.

I can only agree with Michael that this mess happened many years ago. We are now 6 major releases further, stabilized a lot of stuff and made it more robust.

I think you should go ahead with `restic repair snapshots --forget``. Yes indeed, the way the snapshots are accessed is indeed random. It might take a while, since this command is stepping through ~1 million tree records, sized at ~16 GiB. The damage to the repository is really the files in those 3 trees: 8a2d9c58, a37e0905 and f63d7a88. This doesn't look to bad too me. Yes, it takes nearly 1.5 hours to wade through this repository, but it is nearly 3 TiB in size.

It is also possible that your upload- and download-speeds differ, for me at home it is (2 MB/s vs 8MB/s), so your mileage may vary, as they say.

Silvio, 
if you want to hunt large files in your snapshots, ``restic ls -l {snapshot-ID}`` has now the options ``--sort size --reverse``. By using these options, the big monster files will appear at the top of the display.

Secondly, if you start excluding big files by using ``restic rewrite`` you should see some real gain in terms of used space.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hi Silvio,
``prune --max-unused 0`` might give you "up to" 5% more, but it might take a very long time to run, because it will rearrange all partially used packfiles. I don't know if you have considered this option. ``--max-repack-size`` helps you to stop this everlasting process earlier, but you will have a partially pruned repository.

You still have a version 1 repository. From the ``restic stats --mode debug`` output I derive that your ``--pack-size`` is most likely 8 MiB. Today's repositories have at least 16 MiB as default, and you could have even larger sizes. Converting to a 'version 2' repository could give you more space savings, but it depends very much on the contents of your repository. A 'version 2' repository automatically compresses your data. If a lot of your data is mostly text based, you will gain quite a bit of space. But if your data is mostly pictures (.jpg), videos (.mp4 and the like) and PDFs, you won't gain much by compressing the data.

The metadata in your repository (~16 GiB) will compress well, because it is JSON based, so you will gain a few GiB there, but the big lump is your data. Only you know about your data :-) .
